facts.value: The Sopara relics came from a Buddhist stupa that Bhagvanlal Indraji excavated in 1882. A stone coffer held eight bronzes, relic caskets and fragments of a bowl believed to have been the Buddha's begging bowl.
facts.quote: fragments of a begging bowl believed to have been originally used by Gautama Buddha
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://asiaticsociety.org.in/index.php/holdings/sopara-relics' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'fragments of a begging bowl believed to have been originally used by Gautama Buddha'

facts.value: The coin collection numbers more than 12,000 and includes a 5th century gold coin of Kumaragupta, a very rare gold mohur of Akbar and coins issued by Shivaji.
facts.quote: a 5th century gold coin of Kumaragupta, a very rare gold mohur of Akbar
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://asiaticsociety.org.in/index.php/holdings/coins' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'a 5th century gold coin of Kumaragupta, a very rare gold mohur of Akbar'

facts.value: Sir John Malcolm called the Town Hall that houses the Society the most magnificent structure taste and munificence had yet erected in India.

events.label: Bhagvanlal Indraji excavated the Buddhist stupa at Nala Sopara in 1882.
events.quote: In 1882, Pt. Bhagvanlal Indraji, renowned archaeologist, numismatist, epigraphist and Honorary Fellow of the Society, excavated a Buddhist stupa at Nala Sopara
